newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 lower Monday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, dealers said.
LIFFE cocoa futures were broadly lower early Monday in light trading. July fell 14 stg by the midday pause to 1,040 stg a tonne, while May stood down 13 stg at 1,020 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures erased early gains and ended mostly lower, pressured by speculative profit taking. Benchmark July futures finished down $6 at $1,469 a tonne after ranging from $1,494 to $1,466. Spot May -- which goes off the board in 2-1/2 weeks -- rose $13, to $1,465, while the back months fell $7 to $20.

Technically, traders pegged July support at $1,456, a double bottom on the charts. To the upside, they said July would need to get through $1,476-$1,478 before filling a chart gap between $1,494 and $1,501.

The CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 22 showed non-commercial long positions fell by 799 lots, to 15,738 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 883 lots, to 2,488 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 5,688 lots, to 64,275 lots, while commercial short positions rose by 3,635 lots, to 84,488 lots.
Nonreportable long postions fell by 5,826 lots, to 13,490 lots and nonreportable short positions fell by 3,689 lots, to 6,527 lots.

On the fundamental side, industry sources ib Abidjan said Monday that the Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa main crop (Oct-April) will exceed one million tonnes but is unlikely to match the 1.04-1.05 million tonnes seen in the record 1995/96 season.
Arrivals of cocoa at ports totalled 982,157 tonnes by April 12, compared to 1.03 million by the same date last year, they said.
